Theme

moo verb

also low, bellow, low (of cattle), bellow (of an ox), cows moo, oxen bellow

classical

Traupman 142, 298, 141
Liv. 1.7: cum āctae bovēs mūgīssent (as cited by L&S)

mūgiō, mūgīre, mūgīvī (mūgiī), mūgītum

Conjugation on Wiktionary

Other words

  • boō, boāre — to bellow, roar (of an ox)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 143 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Lewis & Short: early and rare (Plautus, Varro on Ennius), from the root of Greek boāō, cry aloud.

Examples

  • Quid dīcit vacca? — Mū! Vacca mūgit.

    What does the cow say? — Moo! The cow is mooing.composed

  • Bovēs mūgiunt.

    Cattle low.Traupman 288

  • Vaccae mūgiunt.

    Cows moo.Traupman 298

  • Bovēs boant.

    Oxen bellow.Traupman 355

See also cow.

SourcesLewis & Short: boo

Lewis & Short: mugio
